review_notes: I read the whole file and compared the proofs for repeated reasoning. The main candidates were map_mul_left and map_mulVec, the positivity facts about norms of unit determinants, and the measurability blocks inside setLIntegral_comp_mul_left. map_mul_left and map_mulVec share a skeleton: compute the det, show it is nonzero, apply the adic-completion lemma, then rewrite the function. A shared lemma there would only wrap an existing API lemma, so I did not report it. The two measurability blocks (lines 613–615 and 633–636) sit in one proof, so they do not meet the "at least two proofs" criterion. The one real repetition across proofs is the nonvanishing of ofReal ((‖Algebra.norm F d‖^2)⁻¹) for a unit d, in Dinv_ne_zero and cg_ne_zero. It is small, so this finding is modest. I did not compile the proposed lemma.

findings.problem: Dinv_ne_zero (lines 545–548) and cg_ne_zero (lines 593–598) repeat the same argument for a unit d. They unfold ofReal_eq_zero, turn IsUnit d into 0 < ‖Algebra.norm F d‖ through isUnit_iff_norm_ne_zero and norm_pos_iff, and close with positivity. The first instance has d = (mat x).det and the second has d = det of g. The same step 'IsUnit d → 0 < ‖Algebra.norm F d‖' also appears in map_mul_left (line 179) and in hδ0 of isFiniteMeasureOnCompacts_m (around line 665). Each copy re-derives it from isUnit_iff_norm_ne_zero. The statement of cg_ne_zero also repeats the body of Dinv by hand.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one lemma in the KcSemiLocalGLHaar namespace:
`theorem norm_pos_of_isUnit {d : E} (hd : IsUnit d) : 0 < ‖Algebra.norm F d‖ := norm_pos_iff.2 ((isUnit_iff_norm_ne_zero d).1 hd)`.
Add a second lemma:
`theorem ofReal_inv_sq_norm_ne_zero {d : E} (hd : IsUnit d) : ENNReal.ofReal ((‖Algebra.norm F d‖ ^ 2)⁻¹) ≠ 0 := by simp only [ne_eq, ENNReal.ofReal_eq_zero, not_le]; have := norm_pos_of_isUnit hd; positivity`.
Then `Dinv_ne_zero hx := ofReal_inv_sq_norm_ne_zero hx`, since Dinv unfolds definitionally to this form, and `cg_ne_zero g := ofReal_inv_sq_norm_ne_zero (Matrix.isUnits_det_units g)`. Use `norm_pos_of_isUnit` at line 179 and for hδ0 as well. The hypotheses match: both uses supply `IsUnit` of a determinant in E, and no new imports are needed.
findings.benefit: The unit-to-positive-norm and ofReal-nonvanishing argument is stated and proved once instead of in four places. Both nonvanishing lemmas become one-liners, and a future change to the weight, for example a different power of the norm, touches one proof.
